problem.title: InTEn-LOAM KITTI 07: recursive mapped-motion S2S seed (rigid rotation)
problem.question: Does recursively feeding previous final mapped motion into S2S reduce sustained motion loss with one fixed setting?

next_step: Review the uniform full-sequence experiment; repository extension stays default off.

variants.label: Fixed accelerated reference
variants.intent: Inherited07-selected profile, acceleration and row-completion off are identical in both arms. Only the recursive mapped-motion S2S seed differs. Repository extension, default off. Quaternion rotation restoration is fixed in the enabled seed. Prior unprojected00 failure retained; all sequences restarted.
variants.note: InTEn-LOAM paper pipeline (FEF, S2S Alg. 1 with re-association, S2M Alg. 2 with TVF map, DOR gating map insertion); no GT seed. intensity=on mapping=on dor=on mean pairs s2s=1385 s2m=2306 dor points/frame=151; repository acceleration enabled (opt-in, not in the paper); imported full paired experiment; timing is not a standalone speed measurement; actual argv in adjacent native_command.json
variants.readability_note: Adds extra tuning knobs and therefore more command complexity.
variants.extensibility_note: Still stable-interface compatible, but with a larger parameter surface.
variants.decision_reason: One candidate setting is evaluated across all sequences. No per-sequence adoption or default selection; the native option remains off.

host.capture_scope: Shared Docker runtime captured before acquisition, not an individual per-run timestamp.
host.measurement_context: Paired runners;07 reference shares CPUs with parent control and07 candidate runs alone. Raw timing retained but no standalone FPS comparison.
